issue_context.title: systemd.dnssd does not handle local requests
issue_context.body:
### systemd version the issue has been seen with

master commit a3680a4

### Used distribution

ubuntu 24.04

### Linux kernel version used

6.8.0-31-generic

### CPU architectures issue was seen on

x86_64

### Component

systemd-resolved

### Expected behaviour you didn't see

running ISC/bind9 dig on localhost fails but works on another host

- hpz25.local IP is 192.168.0.12

```
$ hostname
ubun4.local
$ dig -p 5353 hpz25.local @192.168.0.12

; <<>> DiG 9.18.24-0ubuntu5-Ubuntu <<>> -p 5353 hpz25.local @192.168.0.12
;; global options: +cmd
;; Got answer:
;; WARNING: .local is reserved for Multicast DNS
;; You are currently testing what happens when an mDNS query is leaked to DNS
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 55708
;; flags: qr aa; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 1, AUTHORITY: 0, ADDITIONAL: 0

;; QUESTION SECTION:
;hpz25.local.                   IN      A

;; ANSWER SECTION:
hpz25.local.            120     IN      A       192.168.0.12

;; Query time: 0 msec
;; SERVER: 192.168.0.12#5353(192.168.0.12) (UDP)
;; WHEN: Thu May 23 12:26:53 CEST 2024
;; MSG SIZE  rcvd: 45
```

### Unexpected behaviour you saw


```
$ hostname
hpz25.local
$ dig -p 5353 hpz25.local @192.168.0.12
;; communications error to 192.168.0.12#5353: timed out
;; communications error to 192.168.0.12#5353: timed out
;; communications error to 192.168.0.12#5353: timed out

; <<>> DiG 9.18.24-0ubuntu5-Ubuntu <<>> -p 5353 hpz25.local @192.168.0.12
;; global options: +cmd
;; no servers could be reached
```

### Steps to reproduce the problem

1. enable MulticastDNS=yes on hpz25.local resolved & networkd
2. cat /etc/systemd/dnssd/ssh.dnssd 
```
[Service]
Name=%H
Type=_ssh._tcp
Port=22
```
3. sudo systemctl restart systemd-resolved.service

The same isssue appears using other mDNS client utilities on the local host:
- mquery from https://github.com/troglobit/mdnsd
- libjdns-dev/noble 2.0.3-3.1build3 ubuntu 24.04

### Additional program output to the terminal or log subsystem illustrating the issue

_No response_

review_comments:
This comment is misleading because it allows sending responses and populating the cache along the way too. Now it's possible to for example send send DNAMEs pointing `local` to some weird stuff from the same machine
```sh
Jul 21 12:27:03 H systemd-resolved[205360]: Received mdns UDP packet of size 36, ifindex=3, ttl=64, fragsize=0, sender=192.168.56.4, destination=192.168.56.4
Jul 21 12:27:03 H systemd-resolved[205360]: Got mDNS reply packet
Jul 21 12:27:03 H systemd-resolved[205360]: Added positive unauthenticated non-confidential shared cache entry for local IN DNAME 120s on eth1/INET/192.168.56.4
```
and get something like
```
resolvectl query ho.local
ho.local: resolve call failed: CNAME loop detected, or CNAME resolving disabled on 'ho.local.local.local.local.local.local.local.local.local.local.local.local.local.local.local.local.local'
```
It's an interesting feature I have to say.
